item.title: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike
item.description:
Throughout Israel’s war on Palestine, doctors Thaer Ahmad and Feroze Sidhwa spent months at Nasser Hospital in the southern Gaza city of Khan Younis, where they provided care as volunteers and survived a raid and an airstrike on the complex. On Wednesday evening, they were in an Uber in New York headed to a screening of their film about their time in Gaza when they realized Nasser was the target of another Israeli airstrike. “They just hit Nasser again,” Ahmad said, turning from the front seat toward Sidhwa. “I think Rizk is dead.” He was referring to Dr. Rizk Abu Shaaira, an experienced surgeon and fixture of the Palestinian medical community whom both had worked alongside at the hospital and who appears in their film “ American Doctor .” When Israel attacked Nasser Hospital on Wednesday — for at least the seventh time since the genocide escalated in 2023 — Abu Shaaira was one of the…

item.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
item.description:
Microsoft was a source of frustration for computer users when it stopped working on Nov. 12, 2026. AP Photo/Michel Euler The Microsoft services outage that began on Nov. 12, 2026, is not like other internet outages. The failure affected the Microsoft 365 suite of productivity services, including the video conferencing and collaboration platform Teams, AI assistant Copilot and, significantly, the Outlook email service. Microsoft reported on Nov. 13 that the company is “continuing to see improvements in service availability” but that “some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery.” Despite decades of predictions about its decline , email remains a central pillar of how organizations function. Password resets, invoices, legal notices and cybersecurity incident response coordination all depend on it. The Microsoft 365 outage affected businesses,…

item.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns to launch pad from orbit – video
item.description:
SpaceX made history by catching the upper stage of the largest and most powerful rocket ever built as a pivotal step for the company in its aim to create the first fully reusable rocket. Starship Flight 15, which launched at 5:47 p.m. ET Friday from Starbase in South Texas, achieved the monumental feat of catching the upper stage — called Starship, or “Ship” — of the rocket using the launch tower’s “chopstick” arms on its return to Earth at 4:20 p.m. ET Saturday. item.description:
Filipino entry, pop and rap song Sobra-Sobra, takes 19-year-old to victory at grand final in Bangkok Carmelle Collado has won the first Eurovision song contest Asia, taking the Philippines’ entry, Sobra-Sobra , to victory in Bangkok on Saturday night, at the first regional edition of the contest to be staged outside Europe. item.title: What we know about Brooklyn building collapse that killed eight people
item.description:
Six adults and two children were killed Wednesday afternoon when a three-story building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue collapsed into a construction site next door. Eighteen other people were injured in the collapse or responding to it. One of them remains in critical condition, Mayor Zohran Mamdani reported at a press conference Thursday afternoon. Many of the people impacted by the collapse are immigrants, the mayor said, including from Trinidad, Colombia and Mexico. One victim was a 26-year-old father from Ecuador, Today reported . José Luis Caguana Cosquillo leaves behind his pregnant wife and their first child. Two of the people killed were construction workers working on the excavation next door at the time of the collapse, City officials said. item.title: ‘We gotta do something’: the coalition that helped elect Scott Colom to Senate
item.description:
Behind the Mississippi senator-elect’s victory is a coalition of groups that didn’t have a lot of money, but had collective power and post-Callais anger Long before national political leaders and media were paying any attention, long before the Louisiana v Callais supreme court decision gutted the Voting Rights Act, Mississippi organizers were working to grow political participation and improve quality of life in a state that often ranks low on its residents’ health and wellbeing. Activists’ momentum contributed to Democrat Scott Colom’s historic upset in the midterm elections. A loose coalition of about a dozen, mostly Black-led nonprofits or initiatives rallied residents after Callais, the April decision that set off a flurry of redistricting efforts across southern states. item.title: Can Netanyahu and Eisenkot form a ‘unity’ government in Israel?
item.description:
Prime ministerial hopeful calls Arab minority ‘an integral part of the Israeli story’ as he seeks to form government Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot condemned a “racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation” against the country’s Arab citizens, after the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, accused Arab parties of electoral fraud without evidence. Netanyahu has repeatedly targeted Arab parties and Palestinian citizens of Israel after his party received a disappointing electoral showing, accusing them of manipulating the election and being linked to Hamas. Israeli electoral authorities have rejected these claims as not being backed by evidence. Continue reading...
